title: How to avoid repetition in Task 2 — strategies that helped me go from 6.0 to 7.5
author: Priya Krishnamurthy
preview: After three attempts at Writing, I finally cracked the coherence issue. The key for me was learning to use referencing (this, these, such) instead of repeating the same nouns.
content: After three attempts at Writing, I finally cracked the coherence issue. The key for me was learning to use referencing (this, these, such) instead of repeating the same nouns across sentences. In addition, I created a personal synonym bank for high-frequency topics: education, environment, crime, and technology. Examiners give huge credit when you demonstrate natural lexical substitutions rather than awkward forced thesaurus lookups.

replyList.author: Nusrat Jahan
replyList.content: Thank you for this advice Priya! The tip about referencing with 'such' and 'these' immediately improved the flow of my essay drafts.

replyList.author: Sarah Ahmed
replyList.content: Spot on Priya. As an instructor, cohesive devices and referential pronouns are the #1 thing examiners look for under criterion CC.

title: Band 8.0 achieved — full breakdown of my 6-month preparation strategy
author: Mohammed Al-Qasim
preview: R: 8.5, L: 8.5, W: 7.5, S: 7.5. Overall 8.0. I want to share everything that worked and what I would do differently.
content: R: 8.5, L: 8.5, W: 7.5, S: 7.5. Overall 8.0. I practiced using authentic Cambridge IELTS 18-21 test audio on this platform daily. For listening, I trained at 1.25x speed so the real test felt relaxed and easy to follow. For reading, skimming the first line of each paragraph before looking at questions saved me at least 10 minutes.

replyList.author: Ayaan Rahman
replyList.content: Huge congratulations Mohammed! The 1.25x listening trick is brilliant, will definitely try it on the IELTS 18 tests here.

title: True/False/Not Given — I finally understand the difference (with examples)
author: Yuki Tanaka
preview: The distinction between False and Not Given tripped me up for months. Here is the mental model that finally clicked for me.
content: Remember: FALSE means the passage directly contradicts the statement. NOT GIVEN means the information cannot be found or verified in the text, even if it feels intuitively true from general knowledge! Always ask: 'Did the author explicitly say the opposite?' If no, and there's no mention, it MUST be NOT GIVEN.
